text: 🇲🇽✊ "The welfare programs are love turned into policy." An ex-president called the seniors' pension "supporting the lazy." Sheinbaum's answer: our elders are heroes and heroines of the homeland. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo In Hidalgo alone, 358,297 seniors receive the universal pension — a constitutional right that rises with inflation every year.

🇲🇽🌎 A U.S. president testified to Mexican courage. Sheinbaum read it back. "I have never seen soldiers as brave as the Mexicans — how they fought to defend their homeland." — Ulysses S. Grant, quoted by President Sheinbaum in Hidalgo The U.S. invasion of 1846–48 took more than half of Mexico's territory. Grant, who fought in that war and later became president, called it deeply unjust.

🇲🇽✊ "When you support those who have the least, the whole country does better." Over 1.1 million people in Hidalgo — more than a third of the state's families — receive direct government support through the Banco del Bienestar, with no intermediaries. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo "For the good of all, first the poor" — the humanist model funded, she said, by rooting out corruption.

🇲🇽🏭 Minimum wage up 154% in real terms in 8 years — and no inflation. For 36 years they warned that raising the minimum wage would bring inflation, devalue the peso, and scare off investment. None of it happened. — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo The peso is among the world's strongest currencies and Mexico is at a record for foreign direct investment.

🇲🇽🌎 "Only the people of Mexico can decide their destiny — no foreign power, no elite." Recalling Morelos and the Sentimientos de la Nación, Sheinbaum returned to the root of independence: "Sovereignty springs from the people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Hidalgo Pachuca, Sept 13, 2026 — the month of the patria, marking 216 years since Hidalgo's call to independence.
📸 Niños Héroes de Chapultepec — 13 de septiembre de 2026, Ciudad de México

🇲🇽🌎 179 years ago, teenage cadets chose death over surrender to a U.S. invasion. Today Mexico honored them. President Claudia Sheinbaum led the commemoration of the Gesta Heroica de Chapultepec — six cadets and two officers of the Colegio Militar who fell defending the castle against the invading U.S. Army in 1847. — 179th Anniversary of the Niños Héroes, Altar a la Patria, Mexico City

🇲🇽⚖️ "The homeland is honored, independence is preserved, and sovereignty is defended." On the 179th anniversary of the U.S. invasion of Mexico, the message from the Altar a la Patria was one line. — Gen. Ricardo Trevilla, Defense Secretary, Mexico City He called that sovereignty — the one the cadets died defending in 1847 — not merely a historical aspiration, but a constitutional mandate.

🇲🇽🌎 The U.S. general who invaded Mexico admitted it — in his own memoirs. "The Mexicans have shown a patriotism we would do well to imitate." — Gen. Ricardo Trevilla, Defense Secretary, quoting Ulysses S. Grant 179 years after the U.S. invasion of 1846–47, Mexico honored the teenage cadets who defended Chapultepec to the death. Grant — a young officer in that war, later U.S. president — wrote those words about the enemy he fought.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico's aim in the U.S. trade talks: strike down the tariffs it calls unjust. President Sheinbaum said the goal is to lift U.S. duties on steel, aluminum and automobiles — which she calls unjust and harmful — and to block a new round Washington has floated under an "overcapacity" argument. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on trade negotiations with the U.S.
